questions.question: Explain what is meant by the negative impact of technology, name the three groups into which impacts are sorted with an example of each, and explain why benefits must be weighed alongside costs.
questions.expected_answer: The negative impact of technology is the set of costs a product imposes that its designers did not intend or weigh: pollution, waste, health damage, lost jobs or skills, unfair distribution of costs and climate effects. Environmental impact: raw material extraction, energy and water in manufacture, pollution, waste and climate effects, such as PET bottles persisting in landfill and the sea. Social impact: who gains and loses, jobs, community health near factories and dumps, costs falling on the poor, such as e-waste from cell phones. Individual impact: safety, health, cost and dependence for the user, such as the sugar in cold drinks. Benefits must be weighed because every product also meets a real need, such as the cell phone connecting millions or the nappy saving hours of washing, and a solution must keep the benefit while cutting the cost.

questions.question: Set out the six steps of a product impact investigation and apply the life-cycle stages to a two-litre PET cold-drink bottle, identifying its most serious impacts.
questions.expected_answer: Steps: describe the product, its materials, users and need; trace its life cycle through raw materials, manufacture, transport and sale, use, and disposal; ask the environment, society and individual questions at each stage; gather evidence from the product, local observation, reliable sources and interviews, recording source and date; judge which impacts are most serious by numbers affected, severity, duration and reversibility; record in a table and summary. Bottle: raw material PET from non-renewable oil with refining emissions; manufacture uses energy and water; transport of heavy liquid uses fuel; use delivers a convenient resealable drink but the sugar causes obesity and tooth decay; disposal sees growing PET recycling that supports waste pickers but much litter blocking drains and reaching the sea, persisting for centuries. Most serious: the health impact of the contents and the litter and landfill burden of the bottle.

questions.question: List the types of solution that can counteract a negative impact with an example of each, and state the three questions used to judge a proposed solution in class discussion.
questions.expected_answer: Change the material (bagasse for polystyrene); change the design to use less, last longer, be repairable or come apart for recycling (phone with replaceable battery, bottle with tethered cap); change the use through reuse or sharing (refillable bottles, washable nappies); change the end of life with collection, recycling, deposit or take-back schemes; change the rules with levies, regulations or bans (plastic bag regulations); change behaviour through education and campaigns. Judge each by: does it reduce the harm; does it keep the benefit; is it practical here in cost, in the systems that exist or could be built, and in what people will actually do.
